# Deferred-Anchor Registry — Production

> The canonical source of truth for every `D-*` anchor cited in `src/` but
> deferred to a future cycle. The leading underscore sorts this file before
> the numbered plans in directory listings — call this out as the registry,
> not a plan. Per-plan §3.1 rows are still the preferred home for anchors
> whose feature area maps cleanly onto a plan; this file catches the orphans
> + cross-cutting anchors that don't belong to any single plan.
>
> **CI/pre-commit guard** (`scripts/check-anchor-registry/check-anchor-registry.{sh,ps1}`): every
> `D-*` identifier appearing in `src/` MUST resolve to a row in this file
> OR a citation in any `.plans/*.md`. Pre-fix this recurred TWICE
> (memory: "the same gap silent-failure caught for MULTI-PAGE-GOT").
> The guard makes the system enforce the discipline — same shape as the
> agnosticism veto + the `CallConv` static_assert.
>
> **★ ANCHOR-NAME RULE — READ BEFORE INVENTING A `D-*` NAME (documented 2026-07-28, TF-C81; it was
> load-bearing and unwritten until it bit).** The guard's regex is
> `D-[A-Z0-9_]+(-[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}` — **`D-` plus THREE OR MORE `-`-separated segments is a
> DEFERRED-WORK ANCHOR and MUST resolve to a row here; a TWO-segment `D-*` name (`D-OPT`) is an
> informal feature label the guard ignores.** So hyphenating a COMPOUND FEATURE WORD silently changes
> the identifier's CLASS: `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYS-INLINE` tripped the guard and had to be renamed
> `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE` to match its sibling `D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE`. The failure surfaces as
> “missing row”, which misdirects you into WRITING a duplicate row instead of FIXING the name.
> **Spell a compound feature word as ONE segment (`ALWAYSINLINE`, `NOINLINE`); reserve hyphens for
> genuine name components; when in doubt, match the sibling anchor already in this file.** Full
> write-up: [[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-NAME-SEGMENT-COUNT-GATE]].
>

> **★★ MEASUREMENT CAVEAT — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY “this will clear N errors” NUMBER IN THIS FILE (2026-07-28, macOS-arm64 predefine-probe cycle).** DSS **abandons a TU at its first hard parse failure**, so a corpus error count is a count of the errors REACHED, never of the defects PRESENT. Clearing an early blocker therefore EXPOSES later ones that were never reached, and a drop in the total is NOT a count of defects fixed. Worked example from this cycle: the 189-TU sqlite build went **213 → 80** total errors when architecture + toolchain predefines were both supplied — that is **NOT 133 defects fixed**; the residual 80 is a NEWLY-EXPOSED population whose composition was unknown until separately measured. It is equally possible for a real fix to make the total go UP (this cycle measured exactly that: toolchain-identity macros ALONE took 213 → 216). Every forward estimate of the form “closing X clears N errors” in any row below MUST be read with this caveat, and every new one MUST carry it. See [[D-MEASURE-FIRST-FAILURE-MASKS-RESIDUAL]] for the citable class row.

> ⚠⚠ **THIS REGISTRY IS ONE OF TWO. IT HOLDS PRODUCTION ROWS ONLY (1357 of them).**
> Its sibling is [`_deferred-anchor-registry-harness.md`](_deferred-anchor-registry-harness.md) (574 rows).
> Split 2026-08-25 on operator instruction: *"2 deferred anchor registry files, one for prod,
> other for tool/harness ... the priority is real errors, not cosmetics"* — one pile of 1890 rows
> made the compiler defects unreadable underneath the test and gate defects.
>
> **THE LINE BETWEEN THEM, so a borderline row is decided by a rule and not by taste:**
> **PRODUCTION** is a defect a USER OF THE COMPILER could hit — it is in the shipped binary or in
> the config that binary reads (front end, preprocessor, semantics, HIR/MIR/LIR, optimiser,
> assembler, linker, object formats, FFI surface, diagnostics, CLI, emitted runtime).
> **HARNESS** is a defect only WE can hit — tests, gates, guards, the cycle machinery, plans,
> scripts, carriages, CI, the example corpus AS a corpus.
> ⚠ `D-CONFIG-*` and `D-DIAG-*` are PRODUCTION deliberately: a `.lang/.target/.format.json`
> document IS the compiler's behaviour in this architecture, and a diagnostic is its output to a
> user. Filing either as tooling would hide real conformance defects in the harness pile, which is
> the exact thing this split exists to stop.
> ⚠ A row's bucket follows the DEFECT, never the instrument that found it: a corpus example that
> reveals a codegen bug files under codegen.
>
> ★ **EVERY CONSUMER GLOBS `_deferred-anchor-registry*.md`** rather than naming two paths, so a
> future third split costs nothing and no reader can silently see only half the registry.

## Anchor Index

**Row shape: EXACTLY four cells — `Anchor`, `Trigger`, `Closing work`, `Cross-refs`.**
A row with fewer cells shifts every following cell one column LEFT; a row with more
has the surplus SILENTLY DROPPED by the renderer. Neither is visible when reading the
raw text, so the count is load-bearing — see `D-PLANS-REGISTRY-MALFORMED-ROW-CELLS`.

Two authoring rules follow from that, both verified against the GitHub renderer:
- **A raw `|` splits a cell EVEN INSIDE BACKTICKS.** To quote an expression, regex or
  alternation containing one, write `\|` — the backslash-escaped form is the *only*
  one that survives inside a code span (an HTML entity does **not**).
- **` ═══ ` inside a cell marks a seam where two cells were joined** when a row
  authored to a wider schema was converged onto these four columns. It is a joint in
  the prose, not a column boundary.

⚠ **APPEND AT END-OF-TABLE, NEVER AT END-OF-FILE.** This registry once carried a
second `## Anchor Index (continued)` table, which existed only because rows had been
appended past the Allowlist over many cycles; its header declared TWO columns, so every
fuller row silently lost its `Closing work` and `Cross-refs`. The 2026-08-25
production/harness split merged both tables, so each file now has exactly ONE index and
the accident cannot recur here -- but the rule that prevents it still has to be obeyed.

That decomposition is sound ONLY for an ACYCLIC canonical→use path; when the use sits in a LOOP, execution WRAPS (Load(iter N) → useBlock tail → back-edge → Load(iter N+1)), so a Store in useBlock's tail clobbers the NEXT iteration's Load. In balance_nonroot the body block holds BOTH the candidate Load and the `store slot3, src+1` — the store is in the unscanned tail. The same-block branch (cse.cpp:327-344, scanning only (canonicalIdx+1, i)) has the IDENTICAL hole. | `D-CSUBSET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-LATENT-SUBSTRATE-SITES` | **⏳ OPEN (found by the TF-C56 code-audit, 2026-07-24) — three DEAD-but-target-blind hard-coded char-signedness classification sites in the substrate.** After TF-C56 the ONE *reachable* char→int promotion decision (`Lowerer::isSignedIntKind`) is target-aware, but three OTHER sites still hard-code bare `char`'s signedness target-blind: `mir_to_lir.cpp:~3806` (Gep runtime-index widen) + `:~7405` (switch-discriminant widen) bucket `Char` as SIGNED→SExt, while `hir_to_mir.cpp:~590` (`mapBinaryOp`) classifies `Char` as UNSIGNED (UDiv/UMod/LShr) — mutually inconsistent AND neither consults `charIsUnsigned`. A calling convention that carries the return address in a LINK REGISTER (AAPCS64 x30) rather than pushing it on the stack (x86_64 `call`; callPushBytes=8) makes x30 live across the whole body of a non-leaf function — every `bl`/`call` clobbers it. The frame logic spilled the `calleeSaved` set (x19–x29) but NOT x30 (deliberately the `linkRegister`, NOT in `calleeSaved`, so it stays un-allocatable), so `main`'s epilogue `ret` returned to the clobbered LR (the address after the last call) → an infinite self-loop whose repeated epilogue `add sp` walked SP off the stack into a guard page → SIGSEGV. **The FFI dispatch was always correct** — `abs(7-49)` returned 42 in x0; the PLT stub (ADRP x16/LDR x17/BR x17) + the GLOB_DAT relocation both worked. **Fix** (`src/lir/lir_callconv.cpp::materializeOneFunc`, agnostic + config-driven): when `hasCalls && cc.linkRegister.has_value()`, fold the link register into `savedRegs` so the existing prologue/epilogue machinery spills it at entry + reloads it before `ret`. ZERO `if(arch/format==…)` — x86_64 (no `linkRegister`) takes the no-op path; the schema's long-declared `linkRegister` field (whose `target_schema.hpp` comment PROMISED "ML7 lowering checks linkRegister.has_value()") is finally consumed. **Pins**: `LirCallconv.NonLeafAarch64FunctionSpillsLinkRegister` (non-leaf SAVES x30 + leaf does NOT; RED-on-disable: revert the fold → x30 absent → fail) + `LirCallconv.NonLeafX8664FunctionHasNoLinkRegisterToSpill` (agnosticism control: x86_64 cc has no linkRegister → no-op path) + the `extern_call_elf` arm64 runtime corpus (now genuinely exit 42 under qemu + native-arm64; was SIGSEGV → CI red — so red-on-disable by construction). **+ HOST-INDEPENDENT BYTE-PIN (2026-06-08, same-day hardening)**: `LirCallconv.NonLeafAarch64FramePrologueEpilogueByteExact` drives the real production tail (legalizeTwoAddress → materializeCallingConvention → assemble) and byte-pins the ASSEMBLED non-leaf prologue+epilogue EXACT — incl. `stur x30,[sp,#16]` (f80103fe) at prologue offset 12 + `ldur x30,[sp,#16]` (f84103fe) reloaded before `ret` — against hand-verified ARM-ARM literals, plus a leaf-control (g spills x28/x29 but no `stur x30`). RED-on-disable DEMONSTRATED (disable the fold → frame 0x20→0x10 → both byte windows diverge). Closes the gap where the COMPOSED frame's byte-correctness was witnessed ONLY by the native-arm64 runtime leg (the per-instruction arm64 byte-pins prove instructions in isolation, never the composed frame). | `D-CPP-ERROR-WARNING` | **✅ CLOSED 2026-07-27 (Cycle TF-C70) — C23 `#error` (6.10.5) + `#warning` (6.10.6), config-driven and REACHABILITY-correct.** Closes gap (1) of [[D-CSUBSET-APPLE-SDK-HEADER-SURFACE]]. Before: both words fell through to `P_PreprocessorUnsupported` ("out of FC13 cycle-1 scope") — **50 hits on the macOS sqlite leg, measured as 49 `#error` + 1 `#warning`** (an earlier note said "50 `#error`"; corrected). ★ **THE CRUX IS REACHABILITY, NOT RECOGNITION.** C 6.10.5 makes an `#error` in a NOT-TAKEN `#if` group silent; Apple's SDK headers use `#error` precisely as the unsupported-configuration guard inside branches skipped on a supported target. An implementation firing on every lexed `#error` would turn all 49 into hard user errors and break EVERY macOS compile — strictly worse than the P0015 it replaced. **MECHANISM (agnostic; no engine identity branch):** two OPTIONAL `PreprocessConfig` words `errorDirective`/`warningDirective` (`readOptWord`, the `pragmaDirective`/`embedDirective`/`lineDirective` pattern — there is no `directives` array to extend), valued in `c-subset.lang.json`; two `else if` arms placed INSIDE `handleDirective`'s dispatch chain **below** the `if (!stackActive()) return end;` gate, which makes dead-branch silence structural rather than checked. The arms must NEVER move into the unconditional `#if`-family block above the gate (that block runs in dead regions on purpose, to keep `condStack_` balanced) — stated as an anti-instruction in the code. Two DISTINCT codes `P_PreprocessorErrorDirective`=0x001E / `P_PreprocessorWarningDirective`=0x001F, because `DiagnosticPolicy::suppress` keys on the CODE — one shared code would make `--suppress` of `#warning` noise also silence every `#error`. `emitPP` gained a defaulted trailing severity param (48 pre-existing call sites byte-unchanged: 51 `emitPP(` lines = 1 definition + 50 calls, minus the 2 new arms); `#warning` = Warning, and `hasErrors()`/`pp.fatal` were verified to let the build proceed through compile→link→run. Operand is a RAW source slice, never macro-expanded (gcc/clang parity); a bare `#error` with no operand is legal (`pp-tokens_opt`) and still fires. `P_PreprocessorErrorDirective` is the FIRST `P_*` member of `unsuppressable_codes` (all 127 prior entries are D_/F_/H_/I_/K_/L_/R_/A_/S_ (the table is 128 with this one)) — a user-authored abort must not be suppressible into a silently-built invalid configuration; a new tier line documents the family break. **★ HONEST NET EFFECT — do not misread the next corpus run:** all 49 `#error` sites are in LIVE branches (DSS predefines no `__GNUC__`/`__clang__`/`__x86_64__`/`__arm64__` — grep-verified 0), so this cycle **re-codes 49 P0015 → 49 P001E at the same 49 sites** rather than clearing them: 153 → ~152. That is the point — the old message was an actively misleading lie ("DSS lacks this directive") sent users hunting a missing feature instead of a genuinely-rejected configuration. **The only site this cycle actually CLEARS is the `#warning` at `sys/cdefs.h:81`** (live under `#if !defined(__GNUC__)`), and since nearly every Apple header includes `sys/cdefs.h`, dropping it from Error to Warning is the load-bearing half. The real closer for the 49 is the compiler/arch identity predefines — §B-decided 2026-07-27 to be its own cycle, tracked under [[D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-PLATFORM-MACROS]] (note it needs a per-**ARCH** gate, which `availableObjectFormats` cannot express today — it keys on object FORMAT). **TESTS: 16 `TfC70*` pins, two-directional by construction** — an implementation that fires on every lexed `#error` is caught by the four silence pins (`#if 0`, `#ifdef` undefined, not-taken `#else`, nested dead-outer/live-inner); one that never fires is caught by the positive twins; a hardcoded `"error"` literal is caught by the REBIND pins (`errorDirective`→`"errr"`, then `#error`→P0015 and `#errr`→P001E — a strip-only test would NOT catch it, which is why the design audit rejected the original plan's version as config-theatre). ★ Two spec errors were caught by the test author and are recorded so they are not re-introduced: (i) the nesting test does NOT uniquely prove `sbStackActive` walks every frame — `sbHandleIf` pushes `thisBranchActive = enclosing && cond`, making the innermost check and the full walk observationally equivalent BY CONSTRUCTION, so no test can separate them; (ii) the originally-specified pre-scan test source was INERT (a dead-branch prose `#define` is never harvested, because the pre-scan's define arm is already `sbStackActive`-gated) and was replaced with three empirically-reproduced sub-cases. ★★ (iii) **A MULTI-FORM COVERAGE MISS, caught only by the corpus author and fixed in-cycle — the most instructive failure of the three.** `directiveOperandText` DROPPED THE CLOSING STRING DELIMITER whenever the operand ENDED in a literal: `#warning "Unsupported compiler detected"` reported `#warning: "Unsupported compiler detected` — no closing quote — violating C23 6.10.5p1/6.10.6's verbatim-pp-tokens requirement **on `sys/cdefs.h:81`, the exact shape that motivated the entire feature**. ROOT CAUSE: the tokenizer splits a literal into a `StringStart` token holding ONLY the opening quote plus a COALESCED BODY token covering the bytes BETWEEN the quotes, so the closing quote belongs to NO token's span and a first..last `SourceSpan::join` stops one byte short. The quote-INCLUDE path already solved this identically (`if (dirEnd < spliced.size() && spliced[dirEnd] == dquote) ++dirEnd;`) — the new helper simply did not copy it. FIX: re-consume the trailing byte, GUARDED on it actually being `"` or `'` so a stray unpaired quote (`#error abc"`, already covered by its StringStart's own span) can never gain a phantom character. ★ WHY ALL 13 PINS MISSED IT: every one used BARE PROSE, and `"abc" tail` also passes because the join ends on `tail` — so the suite was green over a SUBSET of the operand FORMS while the single most important form was broken. This is the §A.5 multi-form trap verbatim: a multi-FORM contract needs a test per FORM, not per site. The obvious reading — "unistd.json is missing a `_SC_` constant" — is **WRONG**, and unistd.json's own `$comment` says so: `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` is DELIBERATELY elf-only (`variants`), because glibc's value is 84 while "Darwin's value DIVERGES (58) and is not yet witnessed", so a macho reference is meant to fail loud rather than fold a guessed constant (the fail-loud-over-guess law, `D-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-AVAILABILITY`). Reading the SQLite source settled it: the call sits in `#ifdef _WIN32 … #elif defined(__APPLE__) → sysctl(CTL_HW/HW_AVAILCPU) … #else → sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) #endif`. **A real Apple toolchain never compiles that `#else` arm.** DSS reached it because `__APPLE__`/`__MACH__` appear NOWHERE in `src/dss-config/` — grep-verified. So the fail-loud was a SYMPTOM of compiling the wrong platform branch, not a missing constant, and "add `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` for macho" would have been a WORKAROUND that cemented the wrong arm. ★★ THE REAL SEVERITY IS SILENT, NOT LOUD: here the wrong branch happened to reference an unavailable constant and failed loudly — lucky. Every OTHER `#ifdef __APPLE__` across a 189-TU corpus (os_unix.c's `F_FULLFSYNC`/`F_PREALLOCATE` paths, mmap/fcntl selection, and any third-party header) silently took the NON-Apple arm and would have compiled to valid-but-wrong-for-the-platform code. A compiler that targets Darwin but does not announce Darwin is a silent-miscompile generator by construction. **FIX (config-only, agnostic, no engine change):** two rows in `c-subset.lang.json` `predefinedMacros` — `{__APPLE__,1,["macho"]}` + `{__MACH__,1,["macho"]}` — using the EXISTING per-entry `availableObjectFormats` filter that c95 added for `_WIN32`/`_WIN64`/`_MSC_VER` on `pe` (unknown format names already fail loud at load via `objectFormatKindFromName`). No engine identity branch; the filter is the shipped mechanism. ALSO in the same pass: `fileno` was gated `["elf"]` in `stdio.json` and is now `["elf","macho"]` — **verified, not assumed**: `MacOSX.sdk/usr/lib/libSystem.B.tbd` exports `_fileno` (and `_fileno_unlocked`), so widening the gate cannot plant an undefined import; pe stays excluded because msvcrt spells it `_fileno`. **TEST:** `Preprocessor.FC15bPredefinedMacrosAreOptOutPerLanguage` strengthened from a pure count pin (22) to 24 **plus an EXACT-SET assertion** that the macho-gated set is precisely `{__APPLE__, __MACH__}` — a count bump alone would have gone inert the moment any other macho macro were added. | FIXED for the two macros + `fileno`. **FOLLOW-ON (expected, not a defect):** defining `__APPLE__` flips every Darwin-guarded arm across the corpus ON for the first time, so the Apple-branch OS surface (`sysctl`/`CTL_HW`/`HW_AVAILCPU` from `<sys/sysctl.h>`, `F_FULLFSYNC`/`F_PREALLOCATE`, …) is now REACHABLE and may need shipped-descriptor coverage it never needed before. That cascade is the CORRECT direction — it is what a real Darwin compile does — and is measured by re-running the corpus. ═══ ★ GENERAL RULE: a target's **platform-announcement macros are part of its ABI contract**, not a nicety — omitting them does not disable platform code, it silently selects the WRONG platform code. Whenever a new target/format is added, predefine what the native toolchains predefine. ★ SECOND RULE, from the misdiagnosis: when a fail-loud fires on a platform-gated constant, check the `#if` arm the construct sits in BEFORE adding the constant — the loud symbol may be evidence that an earlier branch decision was wrong. | [[D-CSUBSET-TCL9-HEADER-CONSTRUCTS]] (the sibling front-end gap from the same run); [[D-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-AVAILABILITY]] (the fail-loud-over-guess law that made this diagnosable instead of silent); [[D-HARNESS-TCL-VERSION-AGNOSTIC]] (the pin that got the compile far enough to expose it); c95 `_WIN32`-for-pe (the precedent this copies); `src/dss-config/sources/c-subset.lang.json` · `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/stdio.json` · `tests/analysis/preprocess/test_preprocessor.cpp` |

The native gcc testfixture fails IDENTICALLY.** Matched control run through the SAME `all` tier: native `... Ok` 3,583,595 vs DSS 3,584,676 / 3,584,674; last test passed `inmemory_journal.swarmvtabfault-1.1-oom-persistent.142` in ALL THREE; same error, and a **byte-identical traceback** differing only in the executable name on line 1. ★ SHARPER THAN A BARE TIE: the fault SCHEDULES coincide exactly — max OOM iteration reached per permutation, native vs DSS, `full` 492/492, `memsubsys1` 541/541, `memsubsys2` 549/549. Neither binary was spared or doomed by a shifted allocation sequence; both inject at the same allocation and leak at the same one. ★ The CRT-mismatch caveat (DSS msvcrt+ucrtbase vs MinGW pure-UCRT) is MOOT here, and the reasoning is worth keeping: it was the first alternative explanation ONLY IF native had SURVIVED. Two runs that AGREE cannot be explained by a variable that DIFFERS between them. ★ MECHANISM, corroborated three ways: (1) the leftover 0-byte `test.db2` deletes cleanly once the process EXITS ⇒ the holder was IN-PROCESS, not an external scanner; (2) it reproduces in a pure gcc build ⇒ sqlite's own code; (3) `test.db` and `test.db1` delete fine and only `test.db2` fails ⇒ the glob-order signature of ONE leaked handle. PRIME SUSPECT `ext/misc/unionvtab.c` — the return of `sqlite3_close()` is IGNORED at lines 470 (`unionCloseSources`), 488 (`unionDisconnect`) and 688 (`unionOpenDatabase` error path), each followed by `pSrc->db = 0`. `sqlite3_close()` returns SQLITE_BUSY and leaves the handle OPEN when statements are unfinalized — precisely the state an OOM-aborted swarmvtab cursor teardown leaves — and zeroing the pointer then makes that connection unreachable for the process lifetime. Linux `unlink()` succeeds on an open file, which is why upstream CI never sees it. ⇒ RESOLUTION: an upstream sqlite-on-Windows defect. It may be classified as a confound — but ONLY with this control as the evidence, and NOT by declaring an ABORTED run green: the abort kills the remaining corpus, so calling it green would claim coverage over files that never ran (the same overstatement caught earlier on the `full` tier). The correct fix is to let the REST of `all` run. ★ NOTE the brief's premise that no bounded reproduction exists is probably WRONG: the failure occurs in the **`inmemory_journal`** permutation, which neither earlier probe exercised (they ran the test standalone and under `permutations.test full swarmvtab%`). `testfixture permutations.test inmemory_journal swarmvtab%` is the untried, minutes-long candidate. **OPEN (created 2026-07-25). The pe64 `all` tier does NOT complete — but the failure is neither a wrong answer nor a crash.** **3,584,676 tests pass with ZERO `Expected:`/`Got:` mismatches**, then the fixture dies on a TCL error, not a signal: `testfixture.exe: error deleting "test.db2": permission denied`, raised from `forcedelete` ← `db_restore` ← `faultsim_restore_and_reopen`, inside `swarmvtabfault-1.1-oom-persistent` (test/swarmvtabfault.test:47 — OOM fault injection at allocation #1,000,000 against the `unionvtab` extension). The immediately preceding ~142 cases of that same test all pass. ★★ **REPRODUCIBILITY CONFIRMED 2026-07-26 — 2 runs of 2, same failure, same place.** Run 1: 3,584,676 `Ok` lines; run 2: 3,584,674 — a two-line delta across 3.58M tests (randomised cases), identical error text, identical test. ⇒ This is a DETERMINISTIC bug, NOT a flake and NOT antivirus. That matters procedurally as much as technically: the FIRST native-toolchain control was run before reproducibility was established and came back VOID — standalone `swarmvtabfault.test` passes on BOTH binaries (956 tests, reaching `.477`, i.e. 3.4x past the `.142` where the full run dies), and all three memory permutations (`full`/`memsubsys1`/`memsubsys2`) diff CLEAN between DSS and gcc with byte-identical allocator totals. A void control is not an acquittal; it only proved no bounded window reproduces it. ★ WHAT THAT VOID CONTROL DID ESTABLISH (a real constraint): iterations 1-141 of the failing test each ran `db_restore` -> `forcedelete test.db*` SUCCESSFULLY, so the leaked handle is acquired DURING `swarmvtabfault`'s own execution, not inherited from an earlier file — the trigger needs allocator/VFS state accumulated across the ~813 preceding files (many register and unregister test VFSes), which is exactly why no bounded window reproduces it. ★ ALSO FLAGGED BY THAT CONTROL — a real flaw in the comparison, not a nitpick: the native binary is NOT CRT-matched. DSS imports `msvcrt.dll` + `ucrtbase.dll` (mid-migration, [[D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION]]); MinGW imports the pure-UCRT `api-ms-win-crt-*` set. If the leak is CRT-mediated, a native binary could survive for a reason unrelated to codegen — the exact trap this arc already fell into once. sqlite's `os_win.c` uses raw Win32 `CreateFileW`/`CloseHandle` for DB files (so the CRT is not in the path for the `test.db2` handle itself), but the Tcl layer and `fopen`-based code such as `ext/misc/fileio.c` DO use it. ★ THE POSIX/WINDOWS SEMANTIC AT ISSUE: Linux `unlink()` succeeds on an OPEN file (the inode survives until the last fd closes), Windows refuses to delete a file that any handle still holds. So a handle that leaks under OOM is INVISIBLE on the elf legs and fatal here — which is exactly why `full`/`all` are green on Linux and this is not. ★★ WHY THIS IS PROBABLY NOT ENVIRONMENTAL, i.e. do NOT dismiss it as antivirus: sqlite's own `tester.tcl` already knows this spot is Windows-fragile — `do_delete_file` retries, and `getFileRetries` returns **50 on Windows** (0 elsewhere) with `getFileRetryDelay` = **100 ms**. That is **50 retries over 5 FULL SECONDS**, and the delete STILL failed. AV "tag-alongs" (the cause sqlite's own comment cites) do not hold a handle for 5 s. The parsimonious reading is a genuinely LEAKED file handle under injected OOM. ★ WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN — run the control BEFORE attributing it: does a NATIVE Windows testfixture survive the same test? The pe64 stack-depth investigation taught this the hard way ([[D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH]] METHOD WARNING): comparing DSS against an unmatched native build produced the WRONG conclusion, and the native binary must be built and driven identically. Candidate causes to separate: (a) DSS/consumer leaks a handle on an OOM unwind path; (b) sqlite-on-Windows genuinely leaks under injected OOM and upstream never sees it because its CI is Linux; (c) something in the mid-flight CRT split ([[D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION]]) — NOTE sqlite's os_win.c uses Win32 `CreateFile`/`CloseHandle` directly, NOT CRT `fopen`, so (c) is a priori unlikely and should be TESTED not assumed; the TCL layer, however, does use CRT/Tcl channel I/O. ═══ Already fired (the pe64 `all` tier is red today). Note `full` (0/979,808) and `veryquick` (0/330,937) are BOTH green — this is `all`-tier-only, so it gates only the deepest claim. | (1) Run the native-testfixture control on `swarmvtabfault.test` alone — cheap, one file, and it decides attribution. (2) Per the outcome: chase the leaking handle on the OOM unwind path, or classify as an upstream-on-Windows confound WITH the control as evidence (never on assertion — "green by relabelling" is forbidden). (3) If it is ours, a fail-loud pin on the close path is the durable fix, not a retry bump. | [[D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH]] · [[D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION]] · sqlite `test/swarmvtabfault.test:47` · `test/tester.tcl` (`do_delete_file`/`getFileRetries`) · commit `dd3adc65` (full tier green) |

Without `MirRebuildHelper.RebuildFunctionPreservesAlwaysInline` the propagation argument could be DELETED and the whole suite would stay green. ★ **THE RULE FOR THE NEXT PER-FUNCTION FACT: how much end-to-end coverage a propagation hop gets depends on HOW MANY TIMES THE PIPELINE RE-CONSULTS THE FLAG. A flag read ONCE is invisible to end-to-end tests after that read; a flag read N times is not. COUNT THE READS before concluding a hop needs no pin of its own — do not reason by analogy from a sibling feature, because the read-count is a property of the PIPELINE's relationship to the flag, not of the flag's plumbing.** This is a SHARPER version of the sibling row's lesson, not a repeat of it. ⭐⭐ **THE DEBUG/RELEASE HONESTY SOLUTION — RECORD IT AS A TECHNIQUE, IT IS REUSABLE BEYOND THIS FEATURE.** The shipped `debug` pipeline is `Identity` only, so there is no inliner and nothing for the attribute to do. Rather than shipping a WIDE claim (“always inlined”) plus an annotation carving debug out, the config row **NARROWS THE CLAIM**: the attribute “exempts the callee from the INLINER'S size-based cost model” — a statement about the INLINER, never about the program, and never the words “always inlined”. Under that framing debug is **not an EXCEPTION but an ENTAILMENT** (no inliner ⇒ no threshold ⇒ vacuous), which is exactly the relationship `noinline` already has with debug read in the other direction. **Pinned in BOTH arms** — `MirLoweringCSubsetLinkage.AlwaysInlineBypassesThresholdInShippedRelease` and `…AlwaysInlineIsInertUnderShippedDebugPipeline` — and the debug test's failure message instructs the next author to update the config row in the SAME commit if debug ever gains an inliner. ★ **The general form, worth applying to any config row whose claim is configuration-dependent: when a feature's claim is false in one shipped configuration, prefer NARROWING the claim until every configuration entails it over ANNOTATING a wide claim with exceptions. An exception list is maintained by hope; an entailment is maintained by the pipeline.** ⭐⭐⭐ **A REFUTED PREMISE, KEPT IN THIS ROW SO IT IS NOT RE-PROPOSED: THE BRIEF ASSERTED THAT CLANG **ERRORS** ON `always_inline` + `noinline` TOGETHER. | `D-CSUBSET-BUILTIN-SHADOWED-BY-PROTOTYPE-REVERTS-TO-EXTERN` | 🔴 **OPEN — normal — created 2026-07-31 (TF-C106), found by the IMPLEMENTING agent while probing, not by a failing gate.** ★ **MEASURED: a builtin declared in `builtinFunctions[]` is SHADOW-ABLE, so a translation unit that merely PROTOTYPES the same name turns every call back into an ORDINARY EXTERN REFERENCE.** The agent reproduced it deliberately: prototyping `_byteswap_ushort` in the TU produced **3× `K_SymbolUndefined`** where the builtin lowering had been emitting `bswap` instructions. ⓘ **Shadowing is the CORRECT C semantics** (a user declaration must win over a compiler builtin — that is why the mechanism exists), so this row is NOT a bug report against the shadowing rule. **THE HAZARD IS THE FAILURE MODE:** the call silently stops being a lowered instruction and becomes a link/load-time dependency on a symbol that, for this family, **DOES NOT EXIST** — `msvcrt.dll` exports no `_byteswap_*` (measured by `objdump -p`, with memcpy/_msize/puts as positive controls), and DSS eager-imports declared symbols, so the pe64 outcome is `STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND (0xC0000139)` AT LOAD rather than a compile error. ⚠ **SQLITE IS SAFE TODAY, and only by a hair:** it reaches these names through `#pragma intrinsic(...)`, which NAMES without DECLARING (`realizationRequestOnly`) — so nothing prototypes them. ★★ **THE LIVE TRAP: a REAL MSVC `<intrin.h>` DOES prototype the whole family, and `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/intrin.json` is deliberately a near-empty stub.** Anyone who "completes" that descriptor by adding the honest prototypes — an obviously reasonable-looking improvement — silently converts every byteswap in the corpus from an instruction into an unresolvable import, and the pe64 leg dies at LOAD with no compile diagnostic. That is precisely the shape [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]] exists to warn about, arriving from the opposite direction. | (1) Put a LOUD warning in `intrin.json`'s `$comment` stating that the `_byteswap_*` / `__builtin_bswap*` family must NEVER be given prototypes there, and WHY (prototype ⇒ shadow ⇒ extern ⇒ eager import ⇒ 0xC0000139 at load, because no CRT exports them). (2) Decide the general policy and make it enforceable: either (a) DIAGNOSE the collision — when a user/descriptor declaration shadows a builtin whose lowering has NO importable symbol behind it, emit a real warning naming both, so the silent conversion becomes visible; or (b) let a descriptor mark such names UNSHADOWABLE. ★ (a) is preferred: it keeps C's shadowing semantics intact and only makes the CONSEQUENCE visible, which is the fail-loud posture this project takes elsewhere. (3) Red-on-disable is cheap and exact: a TU that prototypes `_byteswap_ushort` and calls it must produce the chosen diagnostic; today it produces `K_SymbolUndefined` at best and a LOAD failure at worst. Trigger: FIRED (reproduced on demand); no corpus consumer today. Priority: normal — nothing is broken now, but the trap is baited and the bait looks like an improvement. | [[D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP]] (the family that made it reachable) · [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]] (why an undeclared-but-imported symbol is fatal at LOAD, not link) · `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/intrin.json` (the stub that must stay a stub for this family) |

MEASURED: with an initializer present the declarator resolver takes the c34 init-inference relaxation, DROPS the written `argc` bound and re-sizes the object from the brace list, so by validation time the declared type is a plain `int[3]` — `int a[argc] = {1,2,3}; return sizeof(a);` exits **12** through the shipped CLI while `int a[argc];` exits 4. The prior "leaks per-iteration" rationale was factually wrong for a top-level for-init.) MECHANISM: a for-init VLA is declared ONCE at loop entry and PERSISTS across all iterations; C5 frees it ONLY on the loop-EXIT edges, NEVER on the back-edge (freeing it there = a use-after-free of `a[]` in iteration 2+). `emitStackSaveForVla` accepts a `ForStmt` scope node (single-declarator for-init: `hir.parent(declNode) == ForStmt`); the For driver captures the VLA watermark BEFORE the init (`f.vlaBase`), so the for-init frame sits at exactly `vlaBase` and the BODY block's per-iteration teardown (whose watermark is DEEPER, captured after the init) can never reach it (the depth bookkeeping keeps them distinct). The For driver emits ONE StackRestore at the loop EXIT block (the merge of the cond-false edge + every `break` — a break already restored the body VLAs to the post-init watermark, so both predecessors arrive with SP at the post-init level); `continue` frees only body VLAs (post-init watermark), keeping the for-init live; a `goto` OUT of the loop restores the for-init via the ancestry walk (`vlaFrameEnclosesLabel` treats a ForStmt scope as whole-for). Pins: `ForInitVlaEmitsForScopeTeardownAtLoopExitOnly` (for-init-only → 1 save + 1 restore, NONE on the back-edge) + `ForInitAndBodyVlaTornDownAtDistinctPoints` (for-init + body VLA → 2 restores in DIFFERENT blocks) + the `c99_vla_loop` phase-6 runtime witness (a for-init VLA in a 400000-iteration outer loop, written at k=0 + read at k>0 — catches BOTH a back-edge-free [use-after-free → wrong total] AND a leak [overflow]). Multi-declarator for-init VLAs remain deferred → `D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-MULTIDECL`. |

WHY: cst_to_hir wraps a multi-declarator for-init in a `Block` of VarDecls (whose parent is the ForStmt); that Block is lowered via `lowerForClauseNode` during For phase 0 and drains fully (its own Block-scope teardown fires) BEFORE the loop header/body — so a VLA there would be freed at the END OF THE INIT, before the first iteration (a use-after-free for the whole loop). The single-declarator for-init (`for (int a[n]; …)`, the common form, `hir.parent == ForStmt`) gets full for-scope teardown (D-CSUBSET-VLA-FOR-INIT-SCOPE). Detection: `emitStackSaveForVla` recognizes the wrapper by `hir.kind(scopeNode)==Block && hir.parent(scopeNode)==ForStmt && hir.forInit(that)==scopeNode`. Closing work: give the for-init wrapper Block for-scope (not block-scope) teardown semantics — push its VLAs onto the vlaScopeStack without the Block driver's per-exit restore, and free them at the For driver's loop-exit. Trigger: a real multi-declarator-for-init-VLA need. |

(1) VOCABULARY, `.target.json`: the `jcc` opcode row gains a SECOND encoding variant guarded on ONE `blockref` — x86_64 `0F 8x rel32` with no trailing `E9 rel32` (6 bytes, was 11), arm64 `B.cond` alone as a single `fixedWord` (4 bytes, was 8) — selected by OPERAND COUNT through the existing `operandsMatchGuard`, so no walker, no loader and no diagnostic code changed. (2) TRANSFORM, `lir_peephole`'s new rule R2: when a branch's operand list already agrees with its successor list exactly AND the LAST successor is the next-laid-out block AND `lir_pass_util::declaresFallthroughBranchForm` finds the target spelling the shorter form, the TRAILING BlockRef OPERAND is dropped and BOTH SUCCESSORS ARE KEPT — the CFG is untouched, only the encoder's copy of the edge goes. A target declaring no shorter variant gets no elision, from this pass or any other; there is no arch name, mnemonic or byte anywhere in the rule. Conflating them means a perfectly portable dependency whose manifest merely has not listed arm64 REJECTS an arm64 consumer — the tool refusing work that would have succeeded, with a message that reads as a capability statement while reporting a bookkeeping gap. DSS's OWN output cannot reach it (every atom starts at a distinct offset), which is why nothing in the suite had ever moved. ★ THE MODEL: ONE ATOM, SEVERAL NAMES — and all three halves are load-bearing. (a) The relocation-target REMAP is mandatory: `buildCompoundIndex` declares a `SymbolKind` only for ids that own a body and never reads `m.symbols`, so a reloc naming an alias id is `K_SymbolUndefined` — collapsing without the remap would trade a silent miscompile for a spurious link failure. (c) ROW ORDER is part of the contract: every id-to-row lookup keeps the FIRST row, so alias rows append after the canonical one. Identity ranking: externally-visible over module-private, strong over weak, then lowest symbol id. One implementation, three callers — `resolveEqualOffsetAtomAliases` / `outranksAsAtomIdentity` / `AtomStartCandidate` in `object_atom_coverage.hpp`, in neutral (sectionKey, offset) coordinates with no format branch. ELF slices during its symtab walk so it needs a pre-pass, with a post-walk check that fails loud if pre-pass and slicing ever disagree. ⚠ EQUAL OFFSET WITH DIFFERENT DECLARED EXTENTS IS A NESTING, NOT AN ALIAS, and stays REFUSED naming both symbols — a reloc past the shorter extent belongs unambiguously to the longer, one inside it is claimed by both, and no single atom is right for both. Only ELF can produce it. This also REMOVED A PERMISSION THAT WAS HALF TRUE: the ELF overlap guard had waved equal-start pairs through 'because routing to either is offset-correct' — true of the offset, FALSE of the relocation. ⚠ SEVEN MUTANTS WATCHED, subject-binary mtime confirmed each time. TWO OF THE LANE'S OWN ERRORS ARE THE VALUABLE PART: (1) the ELF remap mutant did NOT red at first, because with addend 0 a pre-existing section-relative redirect reaches the same atom by a longer route and computes an identical residual — the pin was rewritten with an addend of 64, pointing OUTSIDE the body it names, which is the property the remap actually adds (an alias binds BY IDENTITY, the redirect binds BY GEOMETRY and correctly refuses); (2) the extent-conflict refusal compared CONSECUTIVE pairs, which misses a run whose two known extents are not adjacent — no shipped reader mixes stated and derived extents, so it would have looked correct forever. Replaced with a first-stated-extent yardstick and pinned. ⚠ The checked-in `clang_macho_subsections_object.inc` fixture CANNOT witness this defect (its only relocation sits outside the shared span); a second real clang object was captured for it. | Closed — nothing further.
